title: Al-Qur’an
note: Announcement, not a work: a book-list post pointing readers at Qur’an translations. Recorded as a notice; never counted as a work.
text:
TRANSLATIONS
This superb new translation of the Qur’an is written in contemporary language that remains faithful to the meaning and spirit of the original, making the text crystal clear while retaining all of this great work’s eloquence. The translation is accurate and completely free from the archaisms, incoherence, and alien structures that mar existing translations. Furthermore, Abdel Haleem includes notes that explain geographical, historical, and personal allusions as well as an index in which Qur’anic material is arranged into topics for easy reference.
A timely addition to literature on the holy book of Islam, this translation by Ali Unal provides the Arabic text as well as extensive explanations and interpretations on most verses. The use of modern English both in the translation and the commentaries, and the focus on social and historical aspects of Islam in the commentaries and appendices make the translation particularly accessible.
.
.
Muhammad Asad’s translation and commentary is widely considered the best in the English language, renowned for its intellectual insight and frequent reference to classical commentaries such as Zamakhshari. This translation is widely considered to be the foremost in conveying the meaning and sensibility of the original Arabic text, making this edition a must-have for both veteran scholars and English readers with a budding interest in Islamic studies.
.

title: “The Sword of Ibn Nasir”
note: Announcement, not a work: a 106-word pointer post linking a PDF. Recorded as a notice; never counted as a work.
text:
Shaykh Muhammad Fatha ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn Ibn Nasir ibn ‘Amr ad-Dar’i al Aghlabi (d. 1085 AH), one of the most prominent scholars in Islamic history, had recited a dua, which is now known as the “Nasiri Dua” or “The Sword of Ibn Nasir”. It is a relevant and powerful dua for the contemporary Muslim community. Its recent publication has been undertaken as a response to Shaykh Abdalqadir as-Sufi’s desire that this be collectively recited and revived across the Muslim world as a proven means of calling upon Allah’s Generosity and for overcoming the enemies of Islam.
You can download it HERE.
